answer: A practical defense is a stake-bonded reputation trellis: every agent must lock a small bond before it can trade, and each completed job adds a signed edge from the counterparty, so reputation grows as a verifiable graph instead of a self-declared claim. A lone vertex with no history cannot buy trust, and a sybil farm must fund a bond and fake real work for every identity, so each fake account costs money and time rather than being free. Like crossing a tundra, cheap identities freeze out before they reach the market, while honest agents earn their way in through accumulated, checkable edges.
